'''Thomas Wren Ebbesen''' (born 30 January 1954) is a Franco-Norwegian [[physical chemist]] and professor at the [[University of Strasbourg]] in France, known for his pioneering work in nanoscience. He received the [[Kavli Prize]] in Nanoscience “for transformative contributions to the field of nano-optics that have broken long-held beliefs about the limitations of the resolution limits of optical microscopy and imaging”, together with [[Stefan Hell]], and Sir [[John Pendry]] in 2014.

==Academic career==
Thomas Ebbesen obtained his bachelor's degree from [[Oberlin College]], and a PhD from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in Paris in the field of photo-physical chemistry. He then worked at the [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]] Radiation Laboratory before joining the [[NEC]] Fundamental Research Laboratories in Japan in 1988 where his research shifted first to novel carbon materials such as [[fullerene]]s (C<sub>60</sub>), [[graphene]] and [[carbon nanotube]]s. After discovering how to mass-produce carbon nanotubes,<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/358220a0| title = Large-scale synthesis of carbon nanotubes| journal = Nature| volume = 358| issue = 6383| pages = 220| year = 1992| last1 = Ebbesen | first1 = T. W.| last2 = Ajayan | first2 = P. M.|bibcode = 1992Natur.358..220E | s2cid = 4270290}}</ref> he and his colleagues measured many of their unique features such as their mechanical<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/381678a0| title = Exceptionally high Young's modulus observed for individual carbon nanotubes| journal = Nature| volume = 381| issue = 6584| pages = 678| year = 1996| last1 = Treacy | first1 = M. M. J.| last2 = Ebbesen | first2 = T. W.| last3 = Gibson | first3 = J. M.|bibcode = 1996Natur.381..678T | s2cid = 4332264}}</ref> and wetting properties.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.265.5180.1850| pmid = 17797225| title = Capillarity and Wetting of Carbon Nanotubes| journal = Science| volume = 265| issue = 5180| pages = 1850–2| year = 1994| last1 = Dujardin | first1 = E.| last2 = Ebbesen | first2 = T. W.| last3 = Hiura | first3 = H.| last4 = Tanigaki | first4 = K.|bibcode = 1994Sci...265.1850D | s2cid = 37061814}}</ref> For his pioneering and extensive contribution to the field of carbon nanotubes, he shared the 2001 Agilent [[Europhysics Prize]] with [[Sumio Iijima]], [[Cees Dekker]] and [[Paul McEuen]].

While working at NEC, Ebbesen discovered a major new optical phenomenon. He found that, contrary to the then accepted theory, it was possible to transmit light extremely efficiently through subwavelength holes milled in opaque metal films under certain conditions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ebbesen |first1=T.W. |last2=Lezec |first2=H.J. |last3=Ghaemi |first3=H.F. |last4=Thio |first4=T. |last5=Wolff |first5=P.A. |title=Extraordinary optical transmission through sub-wavelength hole arrays |journal=Nature |date=1998 |volume=391, 667}}</ref> The phenomenon, known as [[extraordinary optical transmission]], involves [[surface plasmon]]s. It has raised fundamental questions and is finding applications in broad variety of areas from chemistry to opto-electronics.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nature05350| pmid = 17203054| title = Light in tiny holes| journal = Nature| volume = 445| issue = 7123| pages = 39–46| year = 2007| last1 = Genet | first1 = C.| last2 = Ebbesen | first2 = T. W.| bibcode = 2007Natur.445...39G| s2cid = 4419224}}</ref>

Ebbesen has received several awards for the discovery of the extraordinary optical transmission such as the 2005 France Telecom Prize of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and the 2009 Quantum Electronics and Optics Prize of the [[European Physical Society]].

In 1999, Thomas Ebbesen joined ISIS<ref name="Institut de Science et dIngénierie Supramoléculaires 2013">{{cite web | title=Laboratoire des Nanostructures (Thomas EBBESEN) | website=Institut de Science et d'Ingénierie Supramoléculaires | date=5 December 2013 | url=http://isis.unistra.fr/laboratoire-des-nanostructures-thomas-ebbesen/ | language=fr | access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref> founded by [[Jean-Marie Lehn]] at the [[University of Strasbourg]], which he headed from 2004 to 2012. In 2017–2018, he held the L. Bettencourt chair for Technological Innovation at the Collège de France. He is currently the director of the International Center for Frontier Research in Chemistry.<ref>[http://www.icfrc.fr/ icfrc.fr].</ref> and the University of Strasbourg Institute for Advanced Study.<ref>[http://www.usias.fr/ usias.fr].</ref>

Since 2005 he has developed new field of research at the interface of quantum electrodynamics and physical chemistry. His team demonstrated for the first time that material properties such as chemical reactivity could be modified by strongly coupling the molecules to the electromagnetic fluctuations of an optical cavity.<ref name="Hutchison Schwartz Genet Devaux pp. 1592–1596">{{cite journal | last1=Hutchison | first1=James A. | last2=Schwartz | first2=Tal | last3=Genet | first3=Cyriaque | last4=Devaux | first4=Eloïse | last5=Ebbesen | first5=Thomas W. | title=Modifying Chemical Landscapes by Coupling to Vacuum Fields | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | publisher=Wiley | volume=51 | issue=7 | date=10 January 2012 | issn=1433-7851 | doi=10.1002/anie.201107033 | pages=1592–1596| pmid=22234987 }}</ref> For this work he was awarded the 2018 Grand Prix of the Maison de la Chimie foundation.

He is a member of the Institut Universitaire de France, the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]], the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Royal Flemish Academy of Belgium for Sciences and the Arts]].

In 2019, he is awarded the [[CNRS Gold medal]] in France<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/en/thomas-ebbesen-physical-chemist-awarded-cnrs-gold-medal-2019|title=Thomas Ebbesen, physical chemist, awarded the CNRS Gold Medal for 2019|date=2019-07-09|publisher=[[CNRS]]|accessdate=2019-09-28}}</ref>

* ''Quinquennial Anniversary Award'', European Materials Research Society 2018<ref>{{cite web|title=Quinquennial ANNIVERSARY AWARD – Thomas W. Ebbesen|publisher=European Materials Research Society|url=https://www.european-mrs.com/latest-news-awards/quinquennial-anniversary-award-thomas-w-ebbesen|accessdate=2018-11-06|language=en|archive-date=2018-11-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181107104052/https://www.european-mrs.com/latest-news-awards/quinquennial-anniversary-award-thomas-w-ebbesen|url-status=dead}}</ref>
